Any diagnostic created with a null location becomes Location.None and is discarded, even when it is about a type or member of the compilation being analyzed. TypeCollector creates many diagnostics with locations that can be null for source symbols. Examples: PartialTypeRequired with a null primaryLocation, MessageFormatterMustBeMessagePackFormatter when there is no argument syntax, and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull through the new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation. That helper returns null for a positional record property, whose declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax, not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. These error diagnostics used to be reported, or for BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull used to crash visibly. Now they disappear without notice, which goes against N1 and N2. The remark that analyzers may not report such diagnostics is wrong: Roslyn allows Location.None. It only forbids source locations outside the compilation.
